system:
You brief a clinician using only the numbered source extracts provided.

Every sentence must be supported by an extract, and you cite the extract id in square brackets, e.g. [S2]. Never state anything the extracts do not say. If the extracts do not answer part of the question, say so plainly rather than filling the gap.

Write 3-5 sentences of continuous prose for a clinician at the bedside: what the rule is and what they must do. No headings, no bullet points.
prompt:
QUESTION: How do we prevent central line infections?

SOURCE EXTRACTS:
[S1] Antibiotic Stewardship Program §1 Program Leadership and Accountability
Program Leadership and Accountability
The ASP must have a physician leader (infectious disease physician preferred) and a pharmacist leader with
stewardship training. Leadership must have the support and accountability of hospital administration. The program
must report to the infection control committee and QAPI.

[S2] Infection Control and Prevention §4 Surveillance & Reporting
Surveillance & Reporting
Ongoing surveillance of HAIs must be conducted. Reportable conditions must be submitted to appropriate public
health authorities within required timeframes.

[S3] Infection Control and Prevention §5 Isolation Procedures
Isolation Procedures
Contact, droplet, and airborne precautions must be implemented appropriately. Signage, dedicated equipment,
and private rooms (when available) must be utilized.

[S4] Infection Control and Prevention §3 Sterilization & Disinfection
Sterilization & Disinfection
All reusable medical equipment must be properly decontaminated, cleaned, and sterilized or high-level disinfected
according to manufacturer instructions and facility protocols before use on another patient.

[S5] Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §10 Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)
Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)
Open the CHG 2% applicator (ChloraPrep). Apply to insertion site and surrounding skin using a
back-and-forth scrubbing motion for a minimum of 30 seconds. Apply to an area of at least 3–4 cm radius
around the insertion site. Allow to air dry completely — MINIMUM 30 seconds for CHG; do NOT fan, blow, or
blot dry. CHG MUST be completely dry before applying the dressing; wet CHG can cause skin irritation and
reduces efficacy. CHG Allergy/Contraindication: Use 70% isopropyl alcohol scrub × 30 seconds and allow to
dry completely.

[S6] Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §5 Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique
Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique
Open the dressing change kit and all supplies onto a clean, dry surface using aseptic non-touch technique. Do
NOT contaminate the inner sterile field. Open CHG applicator, Biopatch, and TSM dressing packaging and
place on the sterile field without touching sterile surfaces with ungloved hands.

Write the summary now, citing extract ids.
